note: The studio finishing pass on Carrick Study 3: each judged correction, what and why. scripts/build_candidate.py applies the cut_foot edits by name; the others are constructions in the code named.

edits.reason: f's foot is a slanted stem cut like i's and l's, but the flat-foot test measures against the whole letter's width (the crossbar and hook make f wide), so it took the foot for round and set it 8 units below the baseline. It now sits on the baseline as i, l, n and m do, and fi, fl and ff line up.

N513's accent set has one paired piece, two blocks the size of the set's dot, leaning together under the ring; it is the set's only pair and the only mark a European set needs that is otherwise missing, so it is the diaeresis. It replaces the flyer's two tall wedges, which read as a double quote. The blocks touch at their inner feet on N513 and N47: they are parted there by a 2-pixel cut, and each moved 15 units outward so the pair reads as two dots, not a v, at text sizes.

The small figures and letters were weighted with a rounded offset, which softened every corner of a face that is cut, not written, and shut the 4 of the fractions to a slit 5 to 12 units across. They now take a mitred offset, keeping Carrick's cut corners, and a small counter or opening (the small 3's lower bowl) narrows by at most a quarter of its own width on each side: the 4's counter is 21 units across (14 in the Italic).

The sloped style's hair of extra weight joined the c's cut in the copyright sign to its bowl and the m's strokes in the trade mark to each other (both gaps are narrower than the hair at that size). A sloped glyph whose pieces or counters the hair would change keeps the upright's weight, only narrowed.

% and ‰ were small zeros at their own weight with a thin slash and # had hyphen-weight rules (strokes 68-70 against the 1's 176), so they set half as black as the figures; % and ‰ are now the face's own 0 made small with sides 0.63 of the figure stem and a slash 0.58 of it, and # has bars half the stem (strokes 104-106 and 92).

The bar crossed the c at its middle and shut off a lens of the counter (35 units across, 25 in the Italic) behind it; it now stands at the c's back, just covering the counter's innermost point, so the counter stays one open space and the bar stands 19 units clear of the top terminal (it was 14).

The dot stood 44-45 units above the ascender, so that at 14-16 px ḃ read as b and ḟ as f; as Irish types set it (Baoithín, Colum Cille, Britain's 1963 drawings for an Cló Nua-Rómhánach: Bolger 2017, figs 171, 172 and 181) ḃ's dot now stands beside the ascender over the bowl, and ḋ's and ḟ's above, 70-72 units clear (68-71 in the Italic), with b, d, f + U+0307 composed to match (ccmp).

N513 and N47 print the figures' tops on one line (within 2 px, but the 8) and their feet at different depths, so setting each lowest point on the baseline spread the tops from 517 (the 2) to 565 (the 5 and 7); each is scaled about the baseline to the figure line (550; cut and pointed tops 8 above), and the 8, drawn 12 px taller on both prints, keeps its 617.

glyphs: and every other cut of the Italic
edits.reason: The sloped style's hair of weight narrowed every cut by about 7 units (@ 12 to 3, 9 13 to 6, ¢ 14 to 4, u 19 to 8); nodes beside a cut narrower than 0.22 stem now hold, stepping back by what narrowing and sloping take from it, so each Italic cut is within 2 units of the Regular's (@ 11.6 against 12.3, 9 14.4/13.7, ¢ 17.2/18.6, u 18.3/18.6).

edits.code: scripts/symbols.py (make_symbols: RING_WEIGHT, ARM_WEIGHT, CURRENCY_RADIUS, CURRENCY_REACH, AT_RING_OUT, from "signs")
edits.reason: Third pass. The rings of ¤ and @ and ¤'s arms were drawn at the hyphen's weight (46 and 54 units against figure stems of 176) beside % ‰ # at 0.5 to 0.6 of the stem; the rings are now 0.58 of the figure stem and ¤'s arms 0.55, the family of % and #. ¤'s ring grows from 0.34 to 0.40 of the x-height so that its counter stays open (222 across, was 275); @'s ring is thickened half outward and half inward and its a drawn 0.92 as large at its own weight, so the white between them stays 26 units as before and the line box does not move.

Third pass. The small m of ™ was the m scaled and weighted whole, which closed its strokes' cuts (8 and 13 units in the m) to one join and one 1.4-unit hairline (2 in the Italic) that fills in at any size; it is drawn from the m's own three pieces, each weighted alone, and where two come closer than 13.5 units the left one's arm is cut back along the next stroke's edge, so its strokes stand 12.5 to 12.8 units apart (12.5 in the Italic) as Carrick's cut pieces do.

Fourth pass. £'s foot stood 29 units above the baseline (it ran 29 to 647) and the S of $ 36 above it (36 to 607, its bar -63 to 743), so both floated beside the figures, whose feet are on the baseline. Their heights are the prints': N513 sets £ and $ in its row of & ? !, as tall as they are (£ 115 px above that row's line, against the figures' 96 to 102), and the release follows the prints where they are clear, so each keeps its drawing and size and only its foot moves, as the builder sets a figure's foot: £'s flat foot on the baseline (0 to 618), the S's cut foot 8 below it (-8 to 563), the bar going with it (-107 to 699, inside the line box, 988/-213). £'s strokes and the cut between its foot and its body (26) are as they were. € and ¥ stand on the figure line (0 to 550); ¢ is the c's height with its bar.

Fourth pass. ‹ « were drawn from N513's chevron pointing left (189 by 322 units, repeated 166 on) and › » from the one pointing right (166 by 311, repeated 146 on), so « was 432 wide and » 388, ‹ 265 and › 242, and the pairs did not match. The left chevron is the better drawing, a clear angle with an inner corner and two cut ends where the right one bends like a bracket with a round inside, and the larger: every guillemet is now it, the other direction its mirror image, so each pair has one advance (432 and 265; Italic 422 and 262), sidebearings of 38 a side and one outline turned about (within 0.8% of its ink; the Italic's, slope taken out, within 1.8%).

glyphs: and every pair above the x-height
edits.reason: Fourth pass. f's flag came within 9 to 12 units of the next ascender (fb 9.4, fl and fk 10.5, fh 11.3; Italic fl 8.1, fb 12.0, fh and fk 12.5) after protection kerns of +55 to +80, where Carrick's own ascenders stand 15 (lb) and 18 (ll) apart. Tuam's rule now holds at Carrick's cut: above the x-height every pair stands at least 13.5 apart, the white between Carrick's chiselled pieces (the m's cut 13.3; the third pass parted ™'s strokes at 13.5) as Tuam's 28 is its arch cut. Kerned up in steps of 5: fh 16.3, fl and fk 15.5, fb 14.4 (Italic fh and fk 17.5, fl 18.1, fb 17.0), with ĺ ľ ļ ŀ ḃ ł and after ḟ; ll and lb keep their spacing, which a wider cut would loosen. 491 pairs in the Regular (507 in the Italic) gain 5 (a few 10), nearly all ſ, the slash, brackets, £ (whose hook stands above the x-height) and accents above the x-height beside an ascender (čl and ĩl were 8 apart).

Fourth pass. ' and " were the builder's wedge 140 deep and 112 wide with 0.68 of the ink of ’ (198 by 140), so they set small and grey beside the curly quotes. Scaled whole to ’'s depth, as Tuam's were scaled to its weight, they would carry 1.36 times its ink and stand wider than ’, so the wedge is drawn to ’'s depth about the middle of its top, its top on the quotes' line and its widths at top and foot (0.8 and 0.35 of the period's half width, the builder's taper) kept: 112 by 198 with 0.96 of ’'s ink (Italic 0.97). The primes, made from it, follow.

finishing.what: Noise clean-up, not a judged change of shape: the finished outlines are put on the whole-unit grid without the marks rounding leaves. Joins that rounding bent by 1.5 to 10 degrees are smooth again, pieces under 4 units are folded into one node, extremes get nodes; nothing moves more than 2 units, and corners of 10 degrees or more are untouched.
The sloped style's hair of weight is added by moving the drawing's own nodes rather than by a stroked offset, which nearly doubled the sloped outlines' nodes and left them full of short pieces.

Noise, third pass. The TrueType conversion left a 0.16-unit-square loop in the Italic's ı, i and į at (335, 514): the stem's top corner is a cubic 5 units long whose first handle reaches 10 units, past its end (a hook), and cu2qu's spline for it, within 0.8 units and rounded to the grid, crossed itself. In a glyph whose TrueType outline has such a speck, each cubic within 2 units of it is converted again: one under 8 units long that strays from its chord by no more than the conversion and the grid may (1.5 units) as its chord (this hook, whose TrueType corner becomes one corner 1.2 units from the hook's tip), any other split in two on the same curve so that each half's spline follows it; a result with a speck or an out-and-back point is refused. The cubic outlines do not change, and every other glyph converts exactly as before.

fifth_pass.about: A fourth independent review of the released fonts (font outlines only) found three defects shared by the four faces. Each is corrected by one rule for all of them, in scripts/symbols.py (approx_sign, ring_weight, ring_letters, heavier_ring) and scripts/build2.py (Font2.stack_anchors, bottom_clear, the mark and mkmk features), switched on for the release by scripts/build_candidate.py (APPROX_WHITE, RING_SHARE, MARK_STACKS); the study fonts do not change. Measurements are font units, from the fonts before and after.

approxequal.why: ≈ stood 570 tall (−29..541, below the baseline) against the ='s 257 (127..384), its waves 109 heavy against bars of 79 and 145 apart against the ='s 101; its waves are now drawn at the bars' weight (78, Italic 79), centred on the bars on the 256 axis, 0.7 of the ='s white apart (71, Italic 67): 338 tall (87..425)

rings.why: the third pass drew ¤ and @ in the figures' weight (106, 0.6 of the figure stem) and they are the model; © ® ° were still rings of 40 to 52 beside an o of 223; every ring is now at least half the o, 113 (Italic 119; ¤ and @ gain 7); © and ® grow outward, 550 to 674 tall (Italic 700), because the c's 5-unit cut and the r's joins would close if the letters were made smaller, so they stay as drawn, 23 to 32 from the ring; ° has a counter of 80 by 87 (53 by 60 before), ¤ keeps its 223

marks.why: the ponc's anchor was the only top anchor, so marks followed it, and t's flag (above the x-height) took its marks 22 above it against 43 to 48 on the other letters; no mkmk (x + circumflex + acute: 172 into each other), no anchor on a precomposed letter, the comma below ran through g j y (68 to 83 into them), and U+0323 had no glyph; now top marks stand 43 to 46 clear (t 43, Italic 46), stacks 44 apart, comma and dot below at least 23 clear; one rule in every face: the dot above (U+0307) keeps the anchor the ponc is set by, so ḃ ċ ḋ ḟ ġ ṁ ṗ ṡ ṫ and every base + U+0307 shape exactly as before; every other top mark takes the place the face's accents take on its letters (not the ponc's), raised where the letter's own ink comes closer than the face's accent gap (the white of the precomposed vowels); each precomposed letter carries top, ponc and bottom anchors of its own, so a mark typed after it stands on its accent; an mkmk feature sets a second mark above (or below) the first, the same gap apart; a comma or dot below moves along the line, then down, until it stands clear of a descender; U+0323 (combining dot below) is added, the face's dot

changed.why: every glyph whose outline differs from the fourth pass's fonts, per style (with the added dotbelowcomb); kerning changes only in pairs with one of them, the builder's own method applied to the new shapes; the line box, names and every other outline are unchanged
